questions.question: The age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj. Anuj's grandmother is 5 years younger than his grandfather. The total of age of Anuj's grandmother and grandfather is 107 years. What is the age of Anuj?
questions.solution:
Given,

The age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj.

Let us consider age of Anuj = X

Age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj.

Age of Anuj's grand father = 4X

Anuj's grandmother is 5 years younger than his grandfather.

Age of Anju's grand mother = 4X - 5

The total of age of Anuj's grandmother and grandfather is 107 years.

⇒ (4X - 5) + 4X = 107

⇒ 8X - 5 = 107

⇒ 8X = 112

⇒ X = 14

**∴ Here, the age of Anuj is X = 14 years.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"14 years".**

questions.question:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

Option 1) : + and ÷

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 + 21 - 7 ÷ 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 + 21 - __**7 ÷ 28**__ × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 + 21 - __**0.25 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**63 + 21**__ - 0.75 = 144

⇒ __**84**____** - 0.75**__ = 144

⇒ 83.25 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : × and +

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 ÷ 21 - 7 × 28 + 3 = 144

⇒ __**63 ÷ 21**__ - 7 × 28 + 3 = 144

⇒ 3 - __**7 × 28**__ + 3 = 144

⇒ __**3**__ - 196 __**+ 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**6**____** - 196**__ = 144

⇒ - 190 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : ÷ and –

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 - 21 ÷ 7 + 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 - __**21 ÷ 7**__ + 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 - 3 + __**28 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**63**__ - 3 __**+ 84**__ = 144

⇒ __**147 - 3**__ = 144

⇒ **144 = 144**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 4) : + and –

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 ÷ 21 + 7 - 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ __**63 ÷ 21**__ + 7 - 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 3 + 7 - __**28 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**3 + 7**__ - 84 = 144

⇒ __**10 - 84**__ = 144

⇒ - 74 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"÷ and –".**

questions.question: In which year did the Government of India launch the ‘Central Rural Sanitation Programme’ (‘CRSP’)?
questions.solution:
The correct Answer is __1986__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Central Rural Sanitation Programme, which was started in 1986.
 
• It was one of India’s first efforts to provide safe sanitation in rural areas.
 
• This programme focussed mainly on providing subsidies to people to construct sanitation facilities.
 
• A study done by the government in 1996-97 showed that it was more important to raise awareness about sanitation as a whole rather than to just provide subsidies for construction.
 
• This understanding marked the first shift in the programme.
 
• In 1999, a restructured Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) was initiated to create supply-led sanitation by promoting local sanitary marts and a range of technological options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**​ 

 
• The rural sanitation campaign has the following as its objectives:
 
 
• Accelerate sanitation coverage in rural areas.
 
• Generate a push from the people to get facilities rather than expect the Government to do it (demand-led promotion).
 
• Focus on intensive education and awareness campaigns to ensure that people understand the need for safe sanitation.
 
• Take the scheme beyond rural households to rural schools and nursery schools. Here again, the emphasis was placed on promoting good hygiene practices.
 
• Promote cost-effective and appropriate technologies.
 
• Through all the above, improve the health and quality of life in rural areas.

⇒ n² + 13n − 11n − 143 = 0

⇒ n(n + 13) − 11(n + 13) = 0

⇒ (n − 11)(n + 13) = 0

Since n is a natural number, n cannot be negative. Hence, n = 11.

The two numbers are 11 and (11 + 2) = 13.

Average of the numbers = (11 + 13) ÷ 2 = 12.
